subject: How to read very large fixed width data set with R

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: How to read very large fixed width data set with R
parts:
Hi all

my two questions are as follow: 

1- I have a large fixed width data set (approximately, 600000 rows by 400 columns). i have tried to import it with read.fwf in R but it is very time consuming. any suggestion for my problem to increase speed would be appreciate. my preference is using base R. if it can not be done with base R packages are acceptable.  

2- i want to insert comma between this terms by sprintf("q.%s", seq(1:5)). the results is:

 "q.1"   "q.2"   "q.3"   "q.4"   "q.5"

What i want

"q.1",   "q.2",   "q.3",   "q.4",  "q.5"

Best

messages.author: 5f533b50135a7f86
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: How to read very large fixed width data set with R
parts:
Hello Balal, 

For your first question, check out vroom, which is 50-60 times faster than read.delim():  
https://vroom.r-lib.org

For your second question, sprintf() returns a character vector rather than a single string.  You’ll need to use paste(), like so:  
foo = sprintf(“q.%s”, 1:5)
paste(foo, collapse = “, “)

As an aside, note that 1:5 is already the vector of integers from 1 to 5. No need to wrap them in seq().  To create the same vector using seq(), you want seq(1, 5).  
----

What are you trying to accomplish for Q2? That is, are you looking for text that says "q.1", "q.2", "q.3", "q.4", "q.5"?

If so, try cat(paste0('"', paste0("q.",1:5, collapse="\", \""), '"')) (see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/23585306/insert-comma-between-characters-with-r). 


Thanks,
Erica

--

Graduate Group in Ecology, UC Davis
